pull.title: Update secp256k1 subtree to latest master
pull.body:
This PR updates the libsecp256k1 subtree to https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/commit/a0e2e23a71bf2aaae910f81cb2bd8aa0ae49d544, which includes the following changes:

- bitcoin-core/secp256k1#1996

The update is prompted by:
1. New warnings introduced in Clang 24. bitcoin-core/secp256k1#1998 fixed them in the secp256k1 subtree. A fix for Bitcoin Core is here: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36869.
2. New warnings in CMake >=4.5. bitcoin-core/secp256k1#1996 fixed them in the secp256k1 subtree. A fix for Bitcoin Core is here: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36889.

Fixes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36913 and unlocks the CI.

> Shouldn't this wait for [bitcoin-core/secp256k1#1996](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1996)?

It's unclear when that PR will be reviewed and merged, so I'd rather not block on it. It can be picked up in the next subtree update once it lands.

> It's unclear when that PR will be reviewed and merged

I'd assume soon, given it's going to start causing CI failures for us, and is already broken for anyone using CMake 4.5.0 and `dev-mode` locally? Otherwise I'm not clear what the rush is, to merge this, to then just have to pull again in a day or two to get the CMake fix.

> > It's unclear when that PR will be reviewed and merged
> 
> I'd assume soon, given it's going to start causing CI failures for us, and is already broken for anyone using CMake 4.5.0 and `dev-mode` locally? Otherwise I'm not clear what the rush is, to merge this, to then just have to pull again in a day or two to get the CMake fix.

I'll try to post a review of https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1996 today. 

But if you want to speed this up, the thing that helps us is review from CMake experts. @hebasto is the only regular libsecp256k1 contributor who is deep into CMake (and he can't review his own PR). All I can do is stare at the diff, point my LLM to it, and run some testing to make sure the PR doesn't introduce any badness in the build. That's probably all we need for a build system PR but it's still hard for me to judge these PRs dealing with CMake specifics.

> I'll try to post a review of [bitcoin-core/secp256k1#1996](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1996) today.
> 
> But if you want to speed this up, the thing that helps us is review from CMake experts.

Maybe @purpleKarrot can help?
